text:
CLOSURE ACCEPTED, and my framing on this bead was wrong.

I measured this criterion as a COUNT - "5 of 82 Rd files have examples" - and listed nine functions that lacked one. That was the wrong metric. Your criterion says runnable examples must COVER THE FIRST USER JOURNEY, not that every Rd file carries an example. One example that traverses the journey satisfies it better than nine isolated fragments, and that is what you wrote.

Verified by executing man/plan_crossnobis.Rd verbatim. It is a complete self-contained raw-response journey:

  abstract_domain -> simulated design and coefficients -> RAW response matrices with noise
  -> lm_relation_fit -> compile_frame(searchlights) -> pairing -> plan_crossnobis with
     shrinkage_precision -> crossnobis -> print method -> as.data.frame

Output:

  <effect_crossnobis_view>
    measurements: 3
   measurement crossnobis
             1  10.255026
             2   6.823935
             3   1.976304

That is precisely the "one small self-contained raw-data fixture serving three purposes" I suggested at pass 44, and it closes the substantive concern underneath my count: the raw-fMRI entry path now HAS executable documentation. lm_relation_fit is exercised from simulated response data, the learned metric is exercised, and the print and coercion methods are exercised, all in one runnable block that R CMD check executes.

The count remains 5 of 82 and that is fine. Most Rd files document constructors and internals where an isolated example would add noise rather than coverage.

One residual, not worth reopening this bead: crossnobis still appears zero times in either vignette, so the narrative documentation does not present the capability the last three epics were built around. That is a documentation-completeness question rather than a criterion failure, and it can sit in a follow-up if you think it is worth one.
